recipes.name: Chef John's Hot Spinach Artichoke Dip
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup green onions, white and light green parts only, thinly sliced
1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach , thawed, drained and squeezed dry
salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat; stir in onions and pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are soft, about 5 minutes. Stir garlic into onions and remove from heat.
Mix green onion mixture, spinach, artichoke hearts, cream cheese, Gruyere, Parmigiano-Reggiano, hot sauce, nutmeg, salt, and pepper in a large bowl until combined.
Spoon artichoke mixture into two ramekins. Top each with shredded mozzarella cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until tops are golden brown and bubbling, about 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Hot Spinach Artichoke Dip
raw_recipe.description: This rich, delightful, hot spinach-artichoke dip is the perfect accompaniment for watching a game or as an elegant appetizer.

review.reviewBody: I did not measure the hot sauce in this dish--I just added a couple good shakes of Frank's Hot Sauce. I did not add the nutmeg (my husband does not care for it) and I doubled the mozzerella cheese on the top. I did take Chef John's suggestion and bake this in a bigger dish--I spread it in a 8x8 glass square baking dish. I served this with crusty garlic bread and tortilla chips for the boys and celery/carrot "chips" for me. This dip literally lasted less than 20 minutes. Everyone loved it, especially my husband who swore up and down he dosen't like spinach-artichoke dip. This is some good eats!

I did love this, but to me it barely made 5 stars because following the recipe exactly leads to a "dip" that is just not creamy enough. I hate all store-bought jarred Alfredo sauces, almost anything involving mayo, and don't like too much of a sour cream flavor. Because this recipe eliminated those, it sounded like the perfect option. However, I cheated and added about 1/4 cup sour cream because it was just too thick. It was absolutely perfect that way (still very thick), but only if you don't plan on using chips to dip (they would break easily). I spooned the dip onto toasted baguette slices and it was awesome. I highly recommend serving it in a crock pot on low or warm heat to keep it continually warm, because as soon as it isn't piping hot, it loses its awesome texture and flare. I served it in a casserole dish, which was nice in order to get a nice brown top in the oven, but next time I'm going to try a crock pot to keep it toasty.

This dip was very good. The only ingredient I didn't use was the nutmeg. I didn't know how that would taste and didn't want to risk it. Also, I did not add any salt as all the cheeses had enough. Lastly after cooking the green onion and garlic, I put everything in a crockpot. Everyone thought it was amazing.

Delicious! And not greasy. Will definitely make again. I used fresh baby spinach, boiled it for a minute, drained & put it in the fridge & made it the next day. Squeezed the spinach & chopped it in the bowl with a scissors. I personally like it better than frozen if possible. Yum! Will definitely make it again. Chef John never disappoints.

Great dip but it was so dry it lost a lot of its flavor when using baguette slices. I love Chef John and his recipes. I followed this one to the T and it came out just like the video but my wife and I thought it was much to dry. I added some 1/2 and 1/2 the next day making it a moister, (NOT SOUPY) and cheesier. WOW, it was now a 5 star recipe with all the flavors more intense. Adjust the amount of 1/2 and 1/2 to your preference.

This was delicious. The only time I had this was probably 20 years ago at Applebees. As I recall, theirs was very greasy, like Chef John said most recipes are. 

I had such a craving for this, so I sought out a recipe for NYE. Out of necessity, I had to alter the recipe a bit, but not much. My son ate all the Gruyere when I wasn't looking, so I had to use Gouda instead. I'm not a cheese monger, so I'd probably not notice the difference anyway. The artichokes I had on hand, were jarred and marinated. I didn't want the herbs and oil from that, so I drained, and rinsed with hot water. A little seasoning was left behind, but it tasted great.

I didn't like the way he struggled mixing it up. I questioned why he didn't soften the cream cheese first. I microwaved mine so it was soft, but not runny. That's so much easier.

I served it with stale thin sliced baguette left over from NYE. It was awesome.

Excellent dip! I prefer to bake it, but if oven space is scarce you can use a crock pot. I’ve made it this way twice and it came out great. Set to high it was ready in about 45 minutes, I made sure to stir about halfway through, and wait to add mozzarella until the last 15 minutes. Just remember to heat down to warm or off once heated thoroughly as it will dry out even with the lid on.

Great combination of cheeses. I softened the cream cheese and dice the gruyere because I could only find a block at the store. After mixing all the ingredients together, I decided I wanted more cheese than veggies. I added an extra 4 oz of parmesan and gruyere. Hated to do it, but I also needed the sour cream for fluffiness. I sprinkled mozzarella lightly over the top after having mixed half in with everything else. I don't like the stringiness off mozzarella once it has all baked together, so I did this to avoid pulling it all off the top on the first dip. Overall the flavor was delicious!

I used a boiled ear of corn smashed up instead of artichokes, real spinach (about 3 cups chopped), gouda instead of gruyere, fontina instead of mozzarella. Also, more hot sauce! Being cooped up with COVID, you kinda have to use what ya got. It was fab! Use what you have! Some melty stuff on top, perhaps sour cream instead of cream cheese? And PLEASE, be creative!

Really great dip. I added a quarter of a cup of sour cream for creaminess and a small can of Ortega fire roasted green chilies (everything here in the SW gets green chili added). The taste and texture was amazing.

Agree with the other reviews that said there wasn't enough cheese to the amount of spinach and artichoke. I doubled the cream cheese and shredded cheeses that were mixed in, and it came out perfect! I think the extra cream cheese helped make it a light and fluffy dip, not too heavy! I used whole artichoke hearts (canned) and pulsed them in the food processor as I don't like large chunks of artichoke. Delicious!

This is the only time ever I have given less than 5 stars for Chef John. That being said, the recipe came out exactly as promised, not oily at all. However, it was a *little* too dry for our taste. The flavor was absolutely spot on, but with the absence of the oil/fat from no mayo or sour cream prevented the dip from mixing as much as I prefer. I'm definitely going to make it again, but I'll try it with maybe ¼ cup of sour cream. All said, though, I recommend everyone try it as the recipe is written and then decide if it needs tweaking for your palette. You'll still enjoy it and eat a LOT.
I love this! Eat with Milton’s sea salt crackers DELICIOUS!
Love this recipe

I made it mostly as directed with a few modifications: Because there was so much discussion about not creamy enough, I used a brick and half of low fat crème cheese, 1/4 cup of cottage cheese…didn’t have Gruyère so I subbed out cottage cheese. I also did a couple shakes of Tabasco and buffalo wing sauce. Kept the nutmeg. And I did the broiler step. Came out great.
This is a great recipe. It's a richer dip and doesn't have the tang of dips that include mayo or sour cream. It depends what you like but I thought it was great
I like that it’s more of a spread than a dip and more healthy. I froze 2/3 of it unbaked. Hope it turns out well from the freezer.

Everyone really likes this version. I did add about two tablespoons of sour cream because of the dryness comments. I was preparing it the day before and baking it the following, so I think that helped. Another great Chef John recipe! Thank you

I wanted to try something different than the ususal way to make this dip with mayonaise and sour cream. It always gets so greasy. This recipe is fabulous, not greasy and really tasty. I added some chopped water chestnuts to the recipe to give it a bit of crunch. Definitely 5 stars!
Great recipe exactly as written.
